description.value: The study tested whether frontotemporal dementia preferentially affects the rostral limbic system using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: The aim of this study was to test the hypothesis that the rostral limbic system is selectively affected in FTD.

design.value: Nine FTD patients and 26 healthy controls underwent high resolution 3D MRI, followed by voxel-based morphometric comparison of gray matter between cases and controls.

spans.text: Nine FTD patients and 26 healthy controls underwent high resolution 3D MRI.
The “Compare populations—AnCova” procedure was used to compare the gray matter concentration between cases and controls
Overall dementia severity was assessed with the clinical dementia rating scale (CDR) .

All had the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) administered
The “Compare populations—AnCova” procedure was used to compare the gray matter concentration between cases and controls
Nine FTD patients and 26 healthy controls underwent high resolution 3D MRI.

description.value: Patients diagnosed as FTD on clinical grounds, with behavioral problems and a frontal pattern of cognitive function.

spans.text: Patients were diagnosed as FTD when they presented a pattern of symptoms characterized mainly by behavioral problems (lack of insight, dishinibition, emotional unconcern, impaired personal and social conduct) and by a “frontal” pattern of cognitive function
Nine FTD patients and 26 healthy controls underwent high resolution 3D MRI.

After excluding two patients with progressive aphasia in the absence of other cognitive and behavioral disturbances, one who displayed no deterioration in 3 years, one with very anomalous morphology characterized by ventricles smaller than controls’ and abnormal lobar proportions (a morphological outlier) and one subject whose complete digital data were not available for image processing, 9 FTD subjects remained.

exclusion_criteria.value: Patients with disproportionate language or comprehension impairment and minor behavioral deficits were excluded.

spans.text: Language impairment could be present, but patients with disproportionate language or comprehension impairment and minor behavioral deficits were excluded, as these should be diagnosed as PA or SD .

description.value: Patients’ relatives, mostly spouses, without detectable cognitive deficit and judged not demented.

spans.text: Controls were patients’ relatives (mostly spouses) without detectable cognitive deficit.
All had the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) administered, and were judged not demented by a neurologist and a psychologist involved in the evaluation of the patients.
Nine FTD patients and 26 healthy controls underwent high resolution 3D MRI.

Of the original 31 controls, 27 had MRI images suitable for the volumetric analyses of the present study. One of these was excluded for the development of multiple system atrophy a few years after scanning, and 26 control subjects remained.
